You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()

def f(gi):
    g=[r[:] for r in gi]; H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(x for r in g for x in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    objs=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg]
    objcells=set(objs)
    # object = largest connected component of non-bg
    seen=set(); best=[]
    for o in objs:
        if o in seen: continue
        st=[o]; comp=[]
        while st:
            p=st.pop()
            if p in seen: continue
            seen.add(p); comp.append(p)
            r,c=p
            for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                q=(r+dr,c+dc)
                if 0<=q[0]<H and 0<=q[1]<W and g[q[0]][q[1]]!=bg and q not in seen:
                    st.append(q)
        if len(comp)>len(best): best=comp
    objset=set(best)
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            v=g[r][c]
            if v==bg: continue
            # is it part of object?
            if (r,c) in objset: continue
            # nearest object cell
            best=None; bd=10**9
            for (orow,ocol) in objset:
                d=max(abs(orow-r),abs(ocol-c))
                if d<bd: bd=d; best=(orow,ocol)
            if best is not None:
                out[best[0]][best[1]]=v
    return out

for k in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2']:
    print(k, f(G[k+' input'])==G[k+' output'])
print(json.dumps(f(G['Test input'])))

from collections import Counter
for k in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']:
    di,do=G[k+' input'],G[k+' output']
    H,W=len(di),len(di[0])
    bg=Counter(x for r in di for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    objs=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if di[r][c]!=bg]
    rs=[p[0] for p in objs]; cs=[p[1] for p in objs]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
    chg={(i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if di[i][j]!=do[i][j]}
    print('===',k,'bbox rows',r0,r1,'cols',c0,c1,'nchg',len(chg))
    for (i,j) in sorted(chg):
        print((i,j),'in',di[i][j],'out',do[i][j], '| rel_r=',i-r0,'rel_c=',j-c0)

from collections import Counter
def solve(gi):
    g=[r[:] for r in gi]; H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    bg=Counter(x for r in g for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    objs=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg]
    seen=set(); best=[]
    for o in objs:
        if o in seen: continue
        st=[o]; comp=[]
        while st:
            p=st.pop()
            if p in seen: continue
            seen.add(p); comp.append(p)
            r,c=p
            for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                q=(r+dr,c+dc)
                if 0<=q[0]<H and 0<=q[1]<W and g[q[0]][q[1]]!=bg and q not in seen:
                    st.append(q)
        if len(comp)>len(best): best=comp
    objset=set(best)
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    for (sr,sc),v in {((r,c),g[r][c]) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg and (r,c) not in objset}.items():
        # beams in 4 dirs, stop at first non-bg cell
        for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
            r,c=sr+dr,sc+dc
            while 0<=r<H and 0<=c<W and g[r][c]==bg:
                r+=dr; c+=dc
            if 0<=r<H and 0<=c<W and (r,c) not in objset:
                out[r][c]=v
    return out

for k in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3']:
    print(k, solve(G[k+' input'])==G[k+' output'])
import json
print(json.dumps(solve(G['Test input'])))
